run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:42:30Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend-proxy alert at 01:42:30Z coincides with a Chaos Mesh network-partition experiment series named otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition (Schedule in namespace chaos-mesh), whose NetworkChaos objects were applied at 01:42:20Z to the two email pods and the checkout pod and recovered about 55 s later, repeating every minute through at least 01:49:20Z. checkout's own error spans are client HTTP POST spans to the email service ClusterIP 100.67.49.77:8080 that fail after ~30 s with "dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout", and checkout logs carry the same message for http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation. Because PlaceOrder then took ~30 s, frontend-proxy's ingress timed out at 15.0 s and returned 504, which is the error signal behind the alert (span_name ingress, http.status_code 504). Email pods were Running/Ready with 0 restarts, endpoints for Service email contained both pod IPs, and the email spans that did arrive completed within 1 s, so no email application failure was observed. All flagd flags were defaultVariant off, so no feature-flag fault was active at query time. Remaining uncertainty: the Schedule/NetworkChaos specs could not be read, the alert rule definition was not retrievable, and the end of the experiment series is not observed.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own error-span rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total, status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR) was 0.0084/0.015/0.0074/0/0/0.0038/0.0111/0.0074/0/0.0074 spans/s from 01:25:30 to 01:41:30, then rose to 0.2 at 01:45:30, peaked 0.3519 at 01:47:30, 0.2963 at 01:49:30, 0.3400 at 01:51:30, 0.2914 at 01:53:30 and 0.1031 at 01:55:30, the last returned point.

At 01:42:30Z frontend-proxy had 0.0037 spans/s with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR and 19.64 spans/s with STATUS_CODE_UNSET; the error series were on span_name "ingress" (0.0037/s) while span_name "router frontend egress" had 0 error spans/s.

frontend-proxy's error spans carry error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and http.status_code=504 with duration 15,000,000-15,001,496 us (e.g. span 317f5eeff095f1f6 in trace 9d48a9b96ce8529d9cc951391a1769cd and span 666faaba9e7c6553 in trace 4824dfdd47ada84d818501ec6a6f3c0f).

checkout's own error spans are span_name "HTTP POST" client spans with otel.status_description "dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout" and duration ~30,000,000 us; in trace 4824dfdd47ada84d818501ec6a6f3c0f span ca6b4e8a51522e71 (30,001,065 us, status ERROR) is a child of checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder span ba48f10ba3fa54bc.
In namespace otel-demo Service email has clusterIP 100.67.49.77 with port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, so the timing-out address in checkout's spans is the email Service ClusterIP.

checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs logged "failed to send order confirmation to ... failed POST to email service: Post \"http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation\": dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout" repeatedly between 01:49:54 and 01:50:09, immediately after a run of successful "order confirmation email sent" lines at 01:49:15-01:49:19.

Trace 4824dfdd47ada84d818501ec6a6f3c0f shows the whole request path: load-generator POST 504 ERROR at 15,002,497 us, frontend-proxy ingress 504 ERROR at 15,000,325 us, frontend POST /api/checkout 30,421,456 us (http.status_code 200), frontend grpc CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 30,416,973 us, checkout PlaceOrder 30,416,193 us, and the only failing/slow dependency is checkout's HTTP POST to email at 30,001,065 us with the dial-timeout description; cart, product-catalog, currency, payment, shipping and quote spans in the same trace completed within ~0.28 s.

Chaos Mesh events show Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition (involvedObject.kind=Schedule, namespace chaos-mesh) emitting "Create new object: otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-<suffix>" (reason Spawned) at 01:42:20, 01:43:20, 01:44:20, 01:45:20, 01:46:20, 01:47:20, 01:48:20 and 01:49:20, and each spawned NetworkChaos object logged "Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn", "...otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w" and "...otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs", followed about 55 s later by "Time up according to the duration" and "Successfully recover chaos" (reason Recovered) for the same three pods.

Grouped across all namespaces inside the window, the retained events contain 24 NetworkChaos Applied, 21 NetworkChaos Recovered, 15 FinalizerInited, 8 Started, 7 TimeUp, 90 Updated and 8 Schedule Spawned events in namespace chaos-mesh, plus 45 PodNetworkChaos Updated events in namespace otel-demo; the other event groups concern data-recorders jobs/PVCs and one PersistentVolume VolumeFailedDelete warning.

The earliest chaos-related event in the retained window is the NetworkChaos/Schedule activity at 01:42:20Z, ten seconds before the alert's start time of 2026-11-18T01:42:30Z; the retained event set begins 2026-11-18T01:27:26Z and ends 2026-11-18T01:49:36Z.

In the 01:50:00Z per-service/per-span error breakdown only checkout span_name "HTTP POST" (0.2 spans/s) and frontend-proxy span_name "ingress" (0.3963 spans/s) had substantial error rates; frontend, payment, accounting and fraud-detection were 0, and ad/recommendation showed only single small series (0.0037 and 0 spans/s).

frontend's service-level error-span rate was 0 at every 120 s sample from 01:25:30 to 01:55:30, although its POST /api/checkout and grpc CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans reached ~30.42 s in trace 4824dfdd47ada84d818501ec6a6f3c0f, i.e. latency without an error status on frontend's own spans.

Both email pods (email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w on i-071e7666000f6d243 and email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn on i-0ba95c8c42c78df23) were phase Running, container ready=true with restartCount 0 and no lastState.terminated, and the Endpoints object for Service email listed both pod IPs 100.96.3.218 and 100.96.2.7 on port 8080.

Email's own spans show POST /send_order_confirmation and send_email at 0.3704 spans/s with no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series, and every one of those spans was in the le=1000.0 ms bucket (0.3704/s) with 0.1037/s within 50 ms, so the email requests that reached the service were served in under 1 s.

The flagd-config ConfigMap's demo.flagd.json holds 12 flags (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure), all ENABLED with defaultVariant "off" (emailMemoryLeak off=0, paymentFailure off=0, paymentUnreachable off=false).

The NetworkChaos experiments spawned by Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition partitioned traffic between the checkout pod and the two email pods, which produced checkout's 30 s "dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout" on the email call; that 30 s PlaceOrder then exceeded frontend-proxy's 15 s ingress timeout and surfaced as frontend-proxy's 504 error spans. The direction/selectors of the NetworkChaos spec could not be read, so the mechanism is inferred from the event targets, timing and the failing edge.

The email service does not show its own failure: both pods were Running/Ready with 0 restarts, both were present in Endpoints, and the POST /send_order_confirmation spans that arrived completed within 1 s with no error status, so email application slowness or crashing is not supported by email's own signals.

Feature-flag fault injection through flagd (including emailMemoryLeak, paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable) is rejected as the active cause for the queried period: every flag in flagd-config was in defaultVariant "off".
An email pod crash, restart or OOM is rejected: both email pods show restartCount 0 with no terminated last state, and the deployment's pods stayed Running and Ready throughout the observed window.

gaps: The Chaos Mesh Schedule and NetworkChaos/PodNetworkChaos objects could not be read directly (their kinds are not in the permitted Kubernetes kind list), so the chaos action, direction, selectors and duration are unverified; only event messages name the applied pods and times.
Retained events end at 2026-11-18T01:49:36Z, so whether the Schedule kept spawning experiments after 01:49:20Z, and when the partition series ended, is unknown.

The end of the error episode is uncertain: the 5 m frontend-proxy error rate was still 0.1031 spans/s at 01:55:30 (last point of that query) while a separate 3 m query returned a last point of 0 at 01:54:00 and no samples after; metric data availability ends around 01:54-01:55:30, so post-01:55 behavior is unknown.

The alert's own rule was not retrievable: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for type=alert, so the expression and window that produced the annotation value 0.2444444444444444 are unverified; at 01:42:30Z frontend-proxy's span error rate was only 0.0037 spans/s versus 19.64 spans/s UNSET, which does not reproduce that ratio.

http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and kube-state-metrics series were not found in the queried window (get_metric_names for http_.*, rpc_.*, kube_.* returned no_data), so request-level HTTP error metrics and kube-state-metrics corroboration were unavailable; traces_span_metrics_* was the only usable metric family.
NetworkPolicy and ResourceQuota queries returned no_data (nothing matched the queries), so those candidate causes are unchecked rather than excluded.
Email container logs returned no lines for either email pod between 01:38:00 and 01:56:00, so email-side runtime behaviour could not be confirmed from logs (no lines is not proof of absence).

Email pod memory/CPU resource usage was not measured (no container resource metric series observed), so resource pressure on email cannot be directly excluded, although the flagd emailMemoryLeak flag was off.
No change-history integration is available, so what created the Chaos Mesh Schedule and when it was configured could not be verified.
The 0.2444444444444444 value in the alert annotation, and which frontend-proxy metric/label set it was computed from, remains unexplained by the observed span metrics.
next_steps: Review the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition spec (selector, target, action/mode, duration) and its creation/creation-by identity to confirm the intended partition and its end time.

Compare the Schedule's segment boundaries with frontend-proxy 504 and checkout dial-timeout spans once the chaos-mesh objects are readable, to confirm coincidence versus causality per experiment segment.
Inspect the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule definition for RequestErrorRate (frontend-proxy) to confirm which metric and window produced the reported 0.2444 value.
If the alert continues to fire after the last 01:49:20Z experiment, re-check checkout→email connectivity and the NetworkChaos recovery state, since post-01:49 chaos activity is unknown.
